record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.context_brief: least unpopular matchings in house allocation
record.original_question: In the House Allocation problem with strict or tied applicant preferences, can one obtain a better approximation algorithm for finding a matching of minimum unpopularity factor or minimum unpopularity margin, or alternatively prove tighter inapproximability bounds for these optimization problems?

evidence.quote: future work could explore least unpopular matchings further by finding a better approximation algorithm or proving a tighter inapproximability bound.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the House Allocation problem: an instance consists of a set $A$ of applicants and a set $H$ of houses, together with, for each applicant $a \in A$, a preference list over a subset of $H$ that is either strictly ordered or may contain ties (so each list is a weak ranking of acceptable houses). A matching is an assignment $M \subseteq A \times H$ in which each applicant is matched to at most one acceptable house and each house to at most one applicant.

For two matchings $M$ and $M'$, let $\phi(M,M')$ be the number of applicants who strictly prefer their partner in $M$ to their partner in $M'$ (an applicant unmatched in one and matched in the other prefers the matched one; unacceptable assignments are not allowed). Define:
- the unpopularity factor of $M$ as
$$u(M) = \max_{M' : \phi(M',M) > 0} \frac{\phi(M',M)}{\phi(M,M')},$$
- the unpopularity margin of $M$ as
$$g(M) = \max_{M'} \bigl(\phi(M',M) - \phi(M,M')\bigr).$$
A matching is popular if $u(M) \le 1$ (equivalently $g(M) \le 0$).

The optimization problems Min-Unpopularity-Factor and Min-Unpopularity-Margin ask, given an instance, for a matching minimizing $u(M)$ and $g(M)$ respectively.

Problem: Design an approximation algorithm for Min-Unpopularity-Factor or for Min-Unpopularity-Margin in the House Allocation setting (with strict preferences, or with ties) whose approximation guarantee improves on currently known ratios; or, conversely, establish stronger inapproximability lower bounds for these problems than those currently known.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2023–2025) has produced new approximation results for related unpopularity problems, notably tight approximations for the related Graphical House Allocation and improved unpopularity-factor bounds for (3,3)-hypergraph matchings with one-sided preferences. However, no work appears to have closed the approximability gap for Min-Unpopularity-Factor or Min-Unpopularity-Margin in the classical House Allocation problem, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Tight Approximations for Graphical House Allocation
status_evidence.snippet: Tight approximation results for a related graphical variant of house allocation.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work targets approximation for related house-allocation variants but not directly the unpopularity factor/margin in the classical model.

status_evidence.title: Improved Approximation for Unpopularity in (3,3)-Hypergraph Matching with One-Sided Preferences
status_evidence.snippet: Improved approximation algorithm bounding unpopularity factor for (3,3)-hypergraph matchings.
status_evidence.claim: Progress has been made for hypergraph variants, indicating the underlying optimization problem is still being actively studied.

status_evidence.title: An Algorithm for Matching in a (3,3)-Hypergraph With One-Sided Preferences Having Quadratic Unpopularity Factor
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm guaranteeing unpopularity factor at most d^2 for a hypergraph matching variant.
status_evidence.claim: Continued 2025 work on unpopularity approximation shows the question of improved bounds remains active.
